selection: Sprinklr came for placements in the 7th sem. Round 1 was OA on hackerrank style platform, 2 coding qs (one medium array + one graph bfs thing) and around 15 mcqs on OS and networks. Cutoff was not told but around 25 got shortlisted from like 120. Round 2 was a single long technical interview ~1hr. Started with my intern project at Sprinklr (they asked a lot about how i handled the backend part), then process scheduling, deadlock conditions, paging vs segmentation, and one coding q on LRU cache. Interviewer asked me to dry run on a test case. HR was clubbed in the last 10 mins, mostly about relocation to Gurgaon and PPO conversion discussion. Result came the same night.
preparation: Did striver sheet in 3rd yr summer, leetcode regularly after that. OS i revised from gate smashers videos + galvin notes since they ask a lot of it.
experience: Pretty smooth because i already knew the team from the internship. Offer came as PPO conversion basically, so less stress than others.
advice: Be thorough with OS (scheduling, memory mgmt, sync). They like asking about what u built in ur internship so know every line of it.
tips: If u get a PPO chance, work on one thing properly instead of 5 half things. Mentors write the feedback. Also dont ignore the OA cutoff, i almost slipped on the graph q.

selection: Uber intern hiring for us EEE guys was open only for coding roles so CGPA cutoff was the first filter (they went with 7+). Round 1: OA, 2 coding questions in 90 min, one was a sliding window problem and the other a simple DP on strings. Round 2: technical interview, went through my projects (i had an ML based load forecasting project with LSTM) and they asked why LSTM over simple ARIMA, how i handled overfitting, train test split etc. Round 3: DSA interview, 2 problems on trees and heap, had to code in a shared doc. Round 4: managerial + HR, behavioural stuff like conflict in a team, why uber, what if u dont get the project u want. Took almost 2 weeks to get result which was painful.
preparation: Honestly I did leetcode for 8 months, around 400 problems, mostly mediums. Revised ML basics from andrew ng notes just for the project round.
experience: Super stressful because EEE profile and everyone assumes u dont know DSA, so u have to prove it. But interviewers were nice and gave hints when i got stuck.
advice: Know every metric and decision in ur ML project. Explain the why not just the what.
tips: Non CSE guys should apply to coding roles early, dont wait for core companies. Keep ur resume to 1 page and put only projects u can talk for 15 mins. Ask seniors for mock interviews, it helps a lot. Rejections from earlier companies made me stronger ngl.

selection: Schlumberger (SLB) came on campus for core branches and had a 5 round process, it was a long drawn day. Round 1: online aptitude test (quant, logical, verbal, around 45 mins). Round 2: resume shortlisting + group discussion on some energy transition topic. Round 3: technical interview focused on metallurgy basics, they asked about phase diagrams (iron carbon, what happens at eutectoid), heat treatment processes like annealing vs normalizing, corrosion types, and some NDT methods. Round 4: second technical with a senior engineer who asked about my final year project on coatings and failure analysis, asked how i would investigate a pump shaft failure. Round 5: HR, location flexibility (they ask if u r ok to work in field locations), bond, why oil and gas. Final list came around midnight and i was among the 6 selected.
preparation: Revised physical metallurgy and mechanical behaviour of materials from class notes + callister book. Did aptitude from indiabix and some R S Aggarwal for a week. Practiced explaining my project in simple language to a friend.
experience: Long day but organised. SPOCs got us food lol. I was really nervous in round 4 but it went ok.
advice: They love field flexibility so say u r open to rotational field jobs if u are. Know ur basics cold, specially failure analysis.
tips: For core companies, dont only prepare coding, because there is none. Resume should show core projects and internships. Be honest in HR, they can smell fake enthusiasm.

selection: Goldman Sachs quant dev intern. Round 1 was an online test with aptitude (very tough numerical reasoning, time pressure) plus 2 coding questions on hackerrank, one was a medium DP and another was an array/prefix sum one. Everyone said DSA part was fine but the aptitude part is where many got cut. Round 2 was a zoom technical interview of 45 mins where first they asked 2 probability puzzles (expected number of tosses until HH type) then a graph question where i had to find shortest path with some constraint, then a bit on my resume. Didnt have a separate HR, the interviewer asked basic why quant etc at the end. Result came next morning.
preparation: Practiced probability from a green book style questions and past OA problems. Leetcode ~350 questions. Mock interviews with two seniors who had GS earlier.
experience: Intense but fair. My interviewer was calm and let me think. I messed up one puzzle first time but fixed it after a hint.
advice: Brush up probability and expectation, they love those. Do timed aptitude practice since the speed is the real filter.
tips: AI/DS students should not shy away from quant roles, CGPA and consistency help. Dont over-prepare one company and ignore the rest.

selection: Infosys came as a mass recruiter for all branches so even Meta guys could sit. Round 1: online test, reasoning, quant, verbal and a pseudocode section (~100 mins). Round 2: resume screening based on cgpa and backlogs, they shortlisted around 60 percent. Round 3: technical interview, was basic: introduce urself, what is OOPs, difference between C and C++, a simple SQL query for second highest salary, and why IT as a metallurgy student. I told them about my internship in Infosys itself and they asked what i did there. Round 4: HR round, 10 mins, asking about relocation, bond, shifts. Result came after a week. Selected for Systems Engineer.
preparation: Did aptitude for 10 days from indiabix and some youtube. Revised C basics and SQL. Internship at Infosys in 3rd yr helped, got PPO route also so interviews were lighter.
experience: Easy compared to dream product companies but the waiting time is very annoying.
advice: Nothing special, just prepare basic programming and clear aptitude. Be confident for HR.
tips: Dont take mass recruiters lightly, i know people who got cut because of the verbal section. Keep one safe offer in hand and then aim higher.

selection: ITC visited for core roles. Round 1: aptitude test on campus, quant + reasoning + some general awareness. Then round 2 was HR/managerial interview, 20ish mins, they asked about my hostel life, why ITC, if i can handle plant postings, strengths and weakness, my 2 year plan. No heavy technical questions. They also asked what i know about the mining engineer profile as i am from Metallurgy. Fair question lol, i said i did a course on mineral processing and they were fine with it.
preparation: Aptitude practice for 1 week. Read about ITC businesses (FMCG, hotels, agri) on their website and annual report summary.
experience: Chill mostly. I was nervous because the profile is not exactly my branch but they were okay.
advice: Know the business and be ready for questions about working in remote locations.
tips: Dont limit urself to ur dept alone, apply to related roles. Practise HR answers loudly, helps.

selection: L&T internship for mining students was a small drive. OA first: 30 qs, aptitude + some core mining mcqs like drilling and blasting, rock mechanics, ventilation basics (they asked about methane limits and how auxiliary ventilation works). Cleared by around 20 out of 45. Then one interview where technical + HR were mixed. Panel of 2, asked about my previous mine visit during summer, explosives types (ANFO, emulsion), what is RQD, mine ventilation basics like natural vs mechanical, and then the usual HR stuff, relocation to Pune etc. Interview was ~25 mins.
preparation: Revised mining class notes, specially ventilation and blasting, and solved some past year OA questions that seniors shared. Aptitude from indiabix.
experience: Went fine, panel was friendly. A little unsure because i forgot one formula for rock quality but they moved on.
advice: Core knowledge matters more than CGPA here, revise ventilation and drilling.
tips: Mining branch has fewer companies so apply everywhere, and keep ur summer mine visit details in ur resume. Seniors notes are gold.

selection: Walmart Global Tech for IT. Round 1 OA: 2 coding questions + 10 mcqs (OS, DBMS, a bit of networking). 75 mins total. The coding were a medium on hashmaps and another medium-hard on intervals. Round 2: technical interview 1, a linked list question and then lots of OS (what is a thread vs process, mutex vs semaphore, what happens on a page fault). Round 3: technical interview 2, one design-ish question of a parking lot (low level design) and a tree problem. Round 4: managerial/HR with a senior engineer, talked about projects, why Walmart, how i handle deadlines. Whole thing in a single day roughly, results at night. It was 4 rounds including OA.
preparation: Leetcode + striver, OS from galvin and love babbar videos. For LLD i just watched a few youtube parking lot / BookMyShow design videos.
experience: Went decent. Round 3 was the toughest, i took hints.
advice: Be ready with OS and basic LLD. Communicate clearly while coding, they judge thought process.
tips: Do not memorize solutions, interviewers change the question slightly. Stay hydrated lol the day is long.

selection: Wipro came through a campus drive, i was a Mechanical student sitting for IT service roles because i didnt get anything in core. Only 1 round after the aptitude, i mean the online test was the screening (aptitude + verbal + coding) and then one combined interview (technical + HR). Technical was basic OOPs stuff like what is polymorphism, inheritance with example, difference between abstract class and interface, plus 1 simple pattern printing program. HR asked about relocation and willingness to learn new tech. Result in 2 days. Also i had done the Wipro internship so PPO conversion helped.
preparation: Learnt Java basics from NPTEL + some youtube playlists in 2 months. Aptitude from indiabix.
experience: Easy. Only worry was my coding as i am mech, but they asked only basics.
advice: Be clear on OOPs concepts with real examples.
tips: Mech guys, if u want IT roles start coding from 5th sem itself, dont wait. Dont panic if u dont have any core offer, there is always something.

selection: Atlassian DS intern, a 5 round process that stretched over 3 weeks (honestly tiring). Round 1: resume shortlisting after a take home form. Round 2: OA with 2 problems, one involved data processing with hashmaps and another on a graph. Round 3: technical (DSA) one medium problem and one follow up with optimisation. Round 4: system design, designing a simple rate limiter and notification system, they asked about databases, caching, and how to scale. They also asked CN things like what happens when u type a URL, TCP vs UDP, HTTP codes. Round 5: values/behavioural round with an engineering manager, mostly about projects (i discussed a recommender system) and team situations.
preparation: I focused on DSA + system design primer from github, watched gaurav sen videos. CN from kurose notes and a few interview questions lists.
experience: Long but the interviewers were very kind. Got feedback after the process which was cool.
advice: They value collaboration and communication, say what ur thinking. Prepare projects deeply, they ask many follow ups.
tips: Start prepping system design early even for interns, it is asked more now. Mock interviews with seniors saved me. Also dont forget to sleep :)

selection: TCS digital intern profile. Round 1: TCS NQT style online test, with numerical and verbal sections and 2 coding problems (one was easy, one was a bit tricky with strings). Round 2: advanced test for Digital with 2 harder coding questions. Round 3: technical interview, asked OOPs (4 pillars, overloading vs overriding), basic DBMS (normalization, joins), and why data science as a CDS student. Round 4: managerial + HR round where they checked communication and asked about relocation to Mumbai. Overall took 3-4 days from start to result.
preparation: Did TCS NQT previous papers, a lot of prime video lectures on Java, and DSA basics for the coding rounds. Practiced speaking in english with friends.
experience: Smooth honestly. Interviewers were nice, HR was a little rushed.
advice: Prepare earlier year NQT papers. For digital, coding speed matters.
tips: CGPA above 7.5 helps for digital. Dont be nervous in HR, just be honest. Also bring documents properly, SPOCs get strict.

selection: Microsoft came in 7th sem for placement + PPO conversion for those who interned. Round 1: coding round of 3 questions, 90 mins, i did 2 fully and third partially. Then Round 2: super long interview day, 2 interviews back to back but counted as one on-site. First interview was DSA, a tree problem on lowest common ancestor and then a follow up for a variant with parent pointer. Second one was a mix of OOPs and design: they asked to design a class structure for a library system, discussed SOLID, polymorphism usage, then moved to my ML project and asked how i would deploy the model. Result same night, so PPO was converted.
preparation: Since i had interned there, i just revised DSA (neetcode 150) and OOPs/SOLID principles. Did a mock with a senior from Microsoft.
experience: Surprisingly relaxed because of the intern background. Felt prepared and the interviewers were collaborative.
advice: Write clean code, name variables well, talk through edge cases. OOPs design is a must.
tips: Take the internship seriously, the conversion is mostly based on how u perform there. Dont stress about the interview too much once u have PPO, but still prepare so u dont blank.

selection: Salesforce SDE intern, EEE student. OA was the first thing: 3 coding qs in 100 min, i solved 2 and partially the 3rd. About 30 were shortlisted for interviews. Then Round 2: a technical interview where they spent a lot of time on my projects (i had a web app for IoT energy monitoring) and asked about REST apis, how i stored data, why that database. Round 3: DSA round with 2 questions (a medium on strings and a hard-ish on binary search), i could do the first and got a hint for the second. Result in 2 days.
preparation: Leetcode, around 300 solved, mostly array/string/DP. Built 2 web projects with node and react to have something non-EEE on my resume.
experience: Went fine, interviewers were helpful. I was nervous about being EEE but nobody mentioned it.
advice: Projects matter because they dig deep. Be comfortable explaining design choices.
tips: Dont think your branch limits u. Do put at least 2 real projects, and practice coding on a plain editor not just leetcode.

selection: ZS Associates for placements, 4 rounds. Round 1: aptitude test, mostly quant and logical with a data interpretation section, very time bound. Round 2: resume screening and then a case study/business problem written test (like sales dropped in a region, what would u check). Round 3: interview with puzzle questions (the classic 8 balls, 100 doors, and a probability one) plus few questions on my resume. Round 4: partner/HR round, about why consulting, what are my strengths, what would i do in a team where someone isnt working. They liked structured answers. Metallurgy students were few so they asked why analytics.
preparation: Practiced puzzles from a book (shakuntala devi type) and GFG puzzles. Aptitude from indiabix + some case study youtube videos. Did a mock with a senior in ZS.
experience: Interesting! Different from usual tech rounds. Loved the puzzles part, pretty fun when u get it.
advice: Structure ur thinking out loud (framework) and be clear about why u want analytics roles.
tips: For non CSE, show some analytics exposure (a course, a project in python/SQL). Puzzles are easy to prepare and they are high value.

selection: Fractal DS intern. 5 rounds, honestly lots of rounds for an internship. R1 aptitude + SQL basic test. R2 coding test in python (pandas questions and a simple DP). R3 technical interview on my projects, i had a sentiment analysis project, they asked about tf idf vs embeddings, evaluation metrics, class imbalance. R4 puzzles round: asked 3 puzzles (like the pirates/gold coins one and a probability puzzle), i got only 2 and the interviewer was cool. R5 HR + manager, talk about my interests and why Fractal, 15 mins. Results came 3 days later.
preparation: Revised ML basics, andrew ng + statquest videos, SQL from leetcode database problems. Puzzles from GFG for 4-5 days.
experience: Tiring because of number of rounds but everyone was nice. Puzzles were more fun than stressful.
advice: Be strong with ur projects' fundamentals, not just the libraries.
tips: If u have kaggle stuff mention it. Dont freeze on a puzzle, explain how u think and they give partial credit.

selection: Vedanta core day for ECE. Had 4 rounds. R1 was a written technical test (analog and digital electronics, basic control systems, 30 mcqs). R2 technical interview about analog circuits: op amp applications, difference between BJT and MOSFET, digital: K-map and a small FSM question, plus some power electronics as the profile was design engineer for plant automation. R3 second technical with a senior asking about my embedded project with arduino and PLC exposure (which i had none lol). R4 HR round with relocation, willingness to work in shifts, salary expectations. Final list at night, only 5 selected.
preparation: Revised analog and digital from class notes, did NPTEL control systems videos. Went through gate questions of EC for practice.
experience: Okay overall. R3 got bit awkward because i didnt know PLC but i said honestly that i dont know and they respected that.
advice: Be honest, dont bluff on PLC or SCADA, they have people who know it.
tips: For core ECE jobs in heavy industry, know basic instrumentation and automation. Also CGPA matters for first shortlist. Pay is meh but job is stable.

selection: Fractal came and took Chem students for the analyst profile. R1 aptitude test of 45 mins on quant, logical reasoning and some data interpretation. R2 was a case study round, a business analyst case about customer churn which i did on excel basically, then R3 was a technical interview with SQL and python basics (joins, group by, a simple pandas question) and some questions on ML like what is overfitting, regression vs classification. R4 was a puzzle-heavy interview round with also a few HR questions. I got the sheep/ farmer type puzzle and a trick with 25 horses. Whole process took 2 days.
preparation: Learnt SQL and python from a coursera course in 2 months and did around 20 puzzles. Case studies from youtube.
experience: Fun actually. Nobody asked about chemical engg except in the HR round to ask why leave the core domain.
advice: Have a clear answer for why a non CSE guy wants to go into analytics.
tips: Chemical guys, core openings are low for freshers so skill up in python and sql early. I did mine after 5th sem and it was just about enough.

selection: Adobe SDE for IT dept. Only 2 rounds after resume shortlist: Round 1 was a long technical interview (1 hr 10 mins) with coding on a doc, first question was on binary trees (serialize and deserialize) and then a design question: design a url shortener, they asked about hashing, db choices, collision handling, caching. Also asked basic OS (virtual memory, caching in OS, what is thrashing). Round 2 was a hiring manager round, 30-40 mins, they asked about my projects, internship and a bit on how i work in team, and answered my questions about the team. Result in 2 days. Hardest part was the design question.
preparation: Striver + leetcode, gaurav sen system design videos, OS from a lecture series. Did 3-4 mock interviews.
experience: Pretty good. Interviewer was supportive and tried to steer me when i went off track.
advice: Be good with trees and graphs and know the basics of system design. Adobe cares about clean thinking.
tips: Dont rush into coding, clarify requirements first. Whenever u get stuck say it so they can help. All the best :)

selection: ZS analyst intern. OA was an online test with aptitude, a section of logical reasoning and a case MCQ set, about an hour and half. Then an interview round (R2) that was a business case + resume discussion. R3 another case interview with a manager where u need to structure and estimate a market size (how many laptops sold in India per year type). R4 HR, 15 mins, why ZS and about my ECE background. 4 rounds total with OA counted. Shortlist was 10 out of 80 or so. Result by evening.
preparation: I watched case interview videos and did a bit of market sizing practice with a friend. Aptitude from indiabix. Refreshed excel and basic stats.
experience: It went good but i was scared in the case round, interviewer was very nice though, gave me a hint to structure.
advice: Practice structuring and estimation, speak while thinking. Have a reason for choosing analytics.
tips: Dont mug up frameworks, practice real cases. If u r from ECE dont hide it, relate signal stuff to data analysis lol.

selection: Got Uber intern through referral from a senior, so my resume directly went for the interviews without the OA, which saved a lot of stress. R1: DSA interview (graph problem, then a variant), 45 mins, coded in a shared editor. R2: a system design round, design a ride matching system at high level, and they asked how to handle surge, scale and consistency. Quite open ended, interviewer was guiding. R3: HR + manager round, 30 mins, mostly my resume and about a previous team project, and a few behavioural ones. Result 4 days later.
preparation: Mostly leetcode + design interview prep from youtube. Did mock interviews with the same senior who referred me.
experience: Good. Referral helped to get a chance but the interviews were same difficulty as any other candidate.
advice: Know ur basics of distributed systems (sharding, caching, queues) even if u r an intern.
tips: Ask for referrals politely and early, seniors usually help if u show them ur effort. Just a referral doesnt get u the offer, so prep anyway.

selection: Vedanta internship for Meta students. R1: aptitude test (quant + logical + some basic technical mcq on metallurgy, like Fe-C diagram, heat treatments). R2: group discussion, topic was something like India's mining policy. R3: technical interview, they asked about my project on the wear behavior of coatings, why the tests were done that way, SEM vs optical microscopy. R4: HR round, discussed relocation to Chennai plant, willingness for shifts and my goals. 4 rounds total. 7 offers for internships i think.
preparation: Reviewed physical metallurgy and heat treatment, practised aptitude for 5 days and read about Vedanta's business. Prepared a 2 min intro of my project.
experience: It was okay! GD was weird because people were shouting but i managed to say 2 good points.
advice: For GD, speak in a structured manner and dont interrupt too much. Know the project well.
tips: Companies like these value attitude as much as marks, so be polite and show interest in plant visits. Prepare for location questions.

selection: Coal India internship via a CDC arranged process for Civil. R1: aptitude test (reasoning, english, quant). R2: resume shortlisting, they checked our cgpa and projects. R3: technical interview: basic RCC design (singly vs doubly reinforced beam, what is development length), surveying questions (what is a theodolite, how to do a traverse), plus soil mechanics bits like Atterberg limits. R4: a second technical on my project (design of a small bridge deck in STAAD) with a senior engineer. R5: HR/medical-type conversation on field postings and relocation to Chennai office. In total 5 rounds, spread across two days. Final list of 8 names.
preparation: Revised my notes of RCC, surveying and soil, IS code basics, and watched a few NPTEL lectures. Also practised aptitude. Some seniors gave me a question list.
experience: Interviewers were old school but fair. I was stressed because i fumbled the development length question initially.
advice: Know IS codes basics and ur project in detail. Dont bluff on design problems.
tips: Civil guys, start preparing 2 months before. Get comfortable with at least one software like STAAD or AutoCAD, they like it.

selection: Tata Steel came for mining and it was an intense process. R1: HR screening round to check availability for plant locations (Pune office for design). R2: online aptitude + core test of 60 mins (mining engineering mcqs on rock mechanics, mine surveying, ventilation) with negative marking. R3: technical interview with 2 panelists, asked about slope stability, what is a bench in open cast mining, how ventilation is planned in underground mine, explosives. R4: resume + project discussion round, specifically my work on a mine design project using a software. R5: final HR round with a senior manager, they asked about long term goals and mobility. Results after 2 days.
preparation: Core mining subjects from class notes, rewrote my own formula sheet and looked at the last years' questions. Practiced interviews with a senior in Tata Steel.
experience: A bit exhausting but the process was clean. I liked that panel was patient even when i got stuck.
advice: Core mining depth is expected, especially slope stability and ventilation. Be flexible about location.
tips: Dont take HR lightly, they filter on attitude. Keep things from internships written in a small file so u can recall quickly. Cgpa 7.5+ helps a lot with first shortlist.

selection: Nvidia VLSI role for EEE. Round 1 was a long technical interview (1.5 hrs): digital design (setup/hold, CMOS inverter, timing, clock domain crossing), a little verilog coding (write a FIFO, a mod-5 counter), then C programming and pointer basics, and OS: process vs thread, deadlock. Round 2: another technical with a senior, more DSA flavoured: a linked list reversal and an array question, then asked about computer networks basics (OSI layers, tcp handshake). No separate HR; they asked a few general questions at the end. Total 2 rounds but each very long. Offer came in 2 days.
preparation: Digital design from morris mano and the NPTEL VLSI course, did verilog on hdlbits for 2 weeks, and leetcode easy-medium for 100 questions. OS and CN from gate smashers.
experience: Intense for sure but i learned a lot. The senior was friendly and gave hints for the FIFO.
advice: Be very solid with digital design and CMOS basics, and do not skip basic DSA.
tips: EEE guys targeting VLSI, do HDLBits and one decent project in verilog. Resume should have a design project, not just a mini one.

selection: Texas Instruments for a hardware role (i am EEE). Rounds: R1 online test of 60 mins with aptitude plus circuits and digital and few C output questions. R2 technical interview 1 on analog: op amp, feedback, filter design, then a bit of circuits (thevenin, RLC resonance). R3 technical interview 2 on digital and embedded: FSM, setup hold, a bit of C pointers, an OS question about interrupts, and a DSA easy one on arrays. R4 HR + system design-ish discussion (they asked how i would design a small data logger system, which blocks, power budget). I had interned there in 6th sem and PPO'd, so process was a formality with some conversation. Result in 2 days.
preparation: Analog design from razavi basics, digital from morris mano, C and DSA basic revision on leetcode easy. OS concepts for interrupts from a youtube video.
experience: Pretty alright. My cgpa wasnt great (6.1) so PPO was a blessing, otherwise shortlist would have been tough.
advice: TI values fundamentals strongly, so keep analog and digital clear. Intern performance matters more than CGPA for PPO.
tips: Low cgpa isnt the end. Do an internship and work really well, a good manager review beats marks. Dont lose hope after the 6 sem results.

selection: Hindalco came for Mining GET role. R1: written test, 40 core questions (mine ventilation, mine surveying, mineral economics, rock mechanics) and 20 aptitude. R2: group discussion on a topic like green mining. R3: technical interview, asked about my project on slope stability analysis with numbers, how factor of safety is computed, and some questions on rock bolting. R4: managerial round where they asked about leadership in college clubs and problem solving examples. R5: HR + a short medical (just a questionnaire), about posting willingness in remote areas. Results next morning, 4 of us selected.
preparation: Class notes plus an old question bank from seniors, plus the typical aptitude. Practised GD with friends.
experience: Lengthy but they treated us well. Waiting for results was the worst part.
advice: Show interest in field work, many of us say yes but their body language says no, they notice.
tips: Pay is low for GET but good learning, so decide based on ur goals. Keep ur resume simple and honest. Please dont skip GD practice.

selection: Adobe SDE intern, EEE. Only 2 rounds. R1: online coding test, 2 problems: one on stack and one on dp, 90 mins. R2: interview of 1 hour that was a mix, first they asked CN: what happens when u type a URL, DNS, TCP vs UDP, then a system design for a basic chat app (websockets, db schema, scaling), then 1 ML question related to my project (recommendation using collaborative filtering). Coding in that round was a short one on two pointers. Result after 2 days.
preparation: Leetcode, networking from kurose + youtube, system design from a github primer, ML basics revision for the project.
experience: Super fun interview, it felt more like a discussion. I was less nervous because the interviewer joked a bit.
advice: They like clean fundamentals and discussion. Ask clarifying questions.
tips: Since i am EEE, i invested early in CN + OS to match CS guys. If u r in any non CS branch, show real projects. Sleep well before the interview.

selection: Tower Research quant dev intern. Only one real round after the OA. OA was 2 hrs: 3 coding problems and 10 maths/prob questions on hackerrank, quite hard. Cleared top 15 and then they called for one super intense interview of around 75 mins. Started with puzzles: 2 probability puzzles (expected value with a die, a random walk one) then a coding problem about order book matching, with discussions on complexity and edge cases. Final bit was a few questions on low latency C++ concepts (cache, memory layout) since i had mentioned cpp in my resume. Result the next day.
preparation: Practiced from a probability puzzle book and codeforces for speed, around 200 CF problems. Revised cpp basics: stl, pointers, smart pointers.
experience: Intense and mentally exhausting. Loved the puzzles. I got lucky on one probability question honestly.
advice: Speed in OA is key and the interview is about logic more than syntax. Revise C++ memory concepts if u list it.
tips: If u want quant, start codeforces early and also read probability. Dont decide ur worth by one OA, its a lottery partly.

selection: EY analyst role for mech students. Round 1: online assessment with aptitude, verbal, and some basic excel/data MCQs. Cutoff was high, around 60 cleared from 200. Round 2: a single interview, half HR half technical-ish: they asked about resume, my internship in a manufacturing company, about how i would use data in operations, why EY, willingness to work in consulting hours. No thermodynamics or any core stuff. Result came within a day.
preparation: Aptitude practice 10 days, and learnt excel (pivot tables, vlookup) from youtube. Prepared standard HR questions.
experience: Good. Interviewer was kind and the whole thing felt like a conversation.
advice: Resume must be clean and honest. They hire for communication, so speak clearly.
tips: Mechanical guys, consulting and analytics firms hire in good numbers so keep those in the list. Dont ignore verbal section, it kills lots of people.

selection: JSW Steel internship for Mech (profile said mining engineer, kinda weird, but ok). OA was short: aptitude + basic mechanical mcqs (thermodynamics, strength of materials, fluid mechanics) + a bit of general awareness. Then one HR interview of 15 mins where they asked about my CGPA trend, why steel industry, ready for plant location Kolkata or not, and my hobbies. That was it, only 1 round of interview.
preparation: Revised thermodynamics, SOM and fluid mechanics basics for like 4 days. Searched about JSW online.
experience: Easy, i would say. The HR just wanted to know if i was serious about the plant.
advice: Be ready for plant postings and say yes only if u mean it.
tips: Dont overthink OAs for core companies, they are mostly basic. Reply to SPOC messages quickly, i saw someone miss the slot.

selection: Mu Sigma for Mining dept students, analyst/data profile. OA: aptitude and logical reasoning plus a small puzzle section and a couple of sql/ basic stats mcqs. 1 hour. Next round was a tech + HR interview. They asked 2 puzzles (the bridge crossing torch puzzle and one with water jugs), then asked what is mean/median/standard deviation, how would u explain p-value to a non tech person, and finally about my mining project and why data science. Around 30 mins. Cleared and got the intern offer.
preparation: Did aptitude on indiabix, puzzles from GFG, and stats basics from khan academy videos.
experience: It was chill, interviewer was cool and seemed to care about how I explained things.
advice: Clear stats basics, practice puzzles and be able to explain concepts simply.
tips: Mining guys wanting analytics roles, build a small python project on mining data (dataset on kaggle). It stands out.

selection: Bosch for ECE design engineer role. Round 1: technical interview, they asked about embedded and analog: op amp as comparator, ADC types (SAR vs sigma delta), interrupts in microcontrollers, I2C vs SPI and a small C code question. Round 2: HR with a technical manager; resume discussion including my final year project on motor control using PWM, why Bosch, relocation to Bangalore, bond questions. Resume shortlist was based on cgpa 7.5+ so i was lucky there. Total 2 rounds and result same evening.
preparation: Embedded basics from my course + NPTEL, protocol details from a few youtube videos and my own arduino/STM32 projects. Brushed up analog circuits.
experience: Really good, interviewers were interested in my project and it felt like talking to colleagues.
advice: Have hands on projects in embedded, they care. Protocol basics (I2C/SPI/UART) are frequent.
tips: If u have a project, know every line. If u dont, build something small at least. CGPA above 8.5 helped me a lot.

selection: ITC for Mining placement, 5 rounds in one long day. R1: aptitude + core test online (quant, verbal, DI + 20 core mining mcqs). R2: GD (topic: should companies be allowed to mine in forests). R3: project discussion round, i explained my work on drilling and blasting optimisation, they asked about fragmentation, powder factor. R4: technical interview 2 on underground ventilation and safety regulations. R5: HR, relocation to Jamshedpur, postings in different states, my goals. They announced results next day, 4 selected from 22.
preparation: Reviewed my blasting project, class notes for ventilation, read DGMS rules basics. Practiced GD with friends.
experience: Was tiring but i felt ok. R4 was the hardest, i thought i messed up one question on ventilation pressure.
advice: Know ur project in depth and safety regulations. HR will check how open u are for transfers.
tips: Dont take the GD lightly, many get eliminated there. Write 2-3 points in advance for common topics. Take rest after OA, the day is long.

selection: Tata Steel intern for Mining. R1 OA: 25 aptitude + 25 core mining mcqs (ventilation, rock mechanics, surveying), 45 mins. R2: single technical interview with 2 interviewers, asked about basic open pit planning, bench height, RMR/Q-system and a bit on explosives. Interview about 20 mins. No HR round separately; the interviewers asked some general stuff. Selected people got email the same evening.
preparation: Class notes and a seniors' question bank for core, aptitude on indiabix for a week.
experience: Decent. I knew most of the answers. Nothing too tough but time pressure in OA was real.
advice: Core basics are enough but know rock mass classification properly.
tips: If u have internship in mines already, mention it. They like field exposure. Keep calm and answer slowly.

selection: Deloitte consultant role, EEE (dont ask why lol). R1: aptitude and verbal test, very time bound. R2: group discussion (topic on AI replacing jobs). R3: case interview with puzzles: 2 puzzles (mislabelled boxes puzzle and 3 bulbs 3 switches) and a market sizing case. R4: resume-based interview, asked why a EEE student wants consulting, projects, leadership roles, and how i handle pressure. R5: HR round about salary expectations and relocation to Hyderabad. 5 rounds total. I almost didnt make it because i messed up the GD but got selected somehow.
preparation: Practiced puzzles on GFG, verbal from some english test practice, group discussions with friends in hostel. Prepared a story for why consulting.
experience: Stressful, specifically GD where i froze for a moment. But the rest were nice and fair.
advice: Show structured thinking and communication. Speak up in GD but dont dominate.
tips: Dont be afraid of switching domains, a lot of EEE guys end up in consulting. But get ur resume to show some non-technical stuff like clubs. Pay was lowish for me but fine for a start.

selection: Shell came for Mechanical students for process engineer. R1: OA with aptitude and some core sections (thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics) around 90 mins. R2: resume-based screening/ HR style interview. R3: technical interview where they asked Rankine cycle, entropy, why steam turbines use reheating, pump cavitation, heat exchanger types, and how i would design a basic heat exchanger network. R4: managerial interview (about my internship in a power plant, handling safety, etc). Total 4 rounds, results came in 2 days. Only 3 selected from our batch i think.
preparation: Thermodynamics + heat transfer from class notes and NPTEL, practiced previous aptitude, brushed up on my internship learnings. Mock interview with a senior.
experience: It was a good experience but tough. I fumbled on a pump cavitation question but recovered.
advice: Core thermo and fluid mechanics need to be solid. Safety mindset is a plus.
tips: Read about process industry basics. Have a point about safety and ethics ready, Shell likes that. Also don't forget to ask good questions at the end.

selection: Flipkart DS intern. Just one interview after the OA. OA was 2 DSA questions plus 15 mcqs on DBMS and stats. About 40 shortlisted. Then 1 interview round of 1 hour: first DSA (a medium on sliding window, then a follow up), then SQL (write queries on 2-3 tables with joins and window functions), and DBMS theory (acid, indexing, normalization). Data scientist stuff like ML was surprisingly low. Quick result the same night.
preparation: Leetcode + SQL from datalemur, DBMS from my course and gate smashers.
experience: Went smooth i think, the interviewer was a nice guy.
advice: Do SQL window functions properly. DBMS theory is asked a lot.
tips: Dont ignore SQL, it is a free scoring section for DS. And maintain consistent leetcode, just 2 questions a day.

selection: Atlassian SDE placement. 3 rounds. R1: OA with 2 problems in 90 mins, one was a tricky implementation and another on graphs. R2: DSA-heavy technical interview with two mediums on trees and dp; they asked also about OS stuff like paging, mutex vs semaphore at the end because my resume had a project on a custom shell. R3: values + manager round, talked about teamwork examples, a time i disagreed with someone, and about my internship. Result was announced after 3 days. Overall felt more conversational than a typical product company.
preparation: Striver A2Z, leetcode contests, OS from galvin + a few lecture series. Practised behavioural questions using STAR format.
experience: Good. Atlassian is known for being friendly and that was true for me.
advice: Be ready for values round, its serious. Show ownership and collaboration.
tips: Write ur stories (3-4 of them) beforehand and adapt for any behavioural question. And dont forget to ask about the team culture.

selection: Wipro Turbo / Elite hiring for CDS. R1: online assessment, aptitude + verbal + 2 coding problems (easy and medium). R2: another coding assessment round (advanced) and a written communication test. R3: technical interview (OOPs, DBMS, SQL queries, a coding question using python) with 25 mins. R4: HR interview about relocation and my aspiration. R5: a final verification and discussion round with a manager (resume, my project on a flight price predictor, and communication). So 5 stages in total over about a week. Result came 4 days after the last round.
preparation: Practice coding questions on hackerrank, did SQL, python and OOPs revision. Mock HR with friends.
experience: Okay okay. A lot of rounds but fairly easy. Time taken to get results was annoying.
advice: Be thorough with resume and basic python/SQL. Communication test matters.
tips: Mass recruiters take a long time, so apply to product companies too and dont wait for them. Keep a copy of all documents ready.

selection: Coal India placement for Civil, Design Engineer. R1: aptitude test with 50 mcqs on reasoning, quant, english and general awareness. R2: technical interview: RCC (design of slab, limit state vs working stress method), steel structures (types of connections), geotech (bearing capacity, Terzaghi). R3: HR + senior officer round about postings and my long term plan, and CTC details. Only 3 rounds, but results took a week.
preparation: Class notes of RCC, steel design and geotech, plus a few GATE questions. Aptitude for a week.
experience: Fine overall. The interviewers were experienced and asked practical questions rather than bookish ones.
advice: Be practical in answers (site examples), not only theory.
tips: PSU-type recruiters like straightforward honest answers. Keep an eye on mails and notices for document verification.

selection: Hindalco internship for Mining, 2 rounds. R1: aptitude test, 40 qs (quant, logical, verbal) plus 10 mining basics. R2: interview where they asked about my projects (a mine planning mini project), my summer visit to a coal mine, and basics of ventilation and drilling. About 20 mins and fairly relaxed. They asked if i would be fine with a Mumbai office role in planning rather than field.
preparation: Quick revision of mining basics and aptitude for 5 days. Prepared a short explanation of my mine project.
experience: Easy-ish. I was prepared for harder.
advice: Be flexible about role locations.
tips: Apply to all internships, even those that look basic, because the experience helps for later placement.

selection: TCS for Chemical, via campus mass hiring and i had a PPO from my internship, so the process was shorter. R1: TCS NQT test (aptitude + coding) and i got shortlisted. R2: single interview combining technical and HR: they asked about C basics, OOPs, a SQL query and how i would pick up new tech as a chemical engg student. Then HR asked about location preference (i said Hyderabad), bond, relocation. Result in 3 days.
preparation: I took the TCS NQT mock tests and learnt Java/python basics from YouTube for 6 weeks. Also internship notes.
experience: Easy, honest. Only thing is it was slow.
advice: Practice NQT papers for time. Be sure about location preference.
tips: If u r Chem and u dont get core, dont feel low, IT services are decent entry. Maintain 7.5+ cgpa for shortlisting.

selection: HUL came for Mining and the process was a single main round. OA: aptitude + core test. Then one big interview: panel of 2, asked HR + technical mix. They asked about my blasting/explosives understanding, what I know about HUL (sure they dont have mines but the profile was design engineer for a plant), why i want a plant role, and puzzles (like a cutting cake question). Honestly surprised they asked so few core questions. Result at night.
preparation: Aptitude and some mech basics (strength of materials) as the role was about plant design. Learned about HUL's manufacturing units.
experience: Went okay, my first interview so i was nervous. Interviewers were calm.
advice: Show enthusiasm for operations and design roles, they like that.
tips: Keep ur basics ready from first and second year too, they might ask random stuff. Smile and speak slowly.

selection: Mu Sigma intern, 5 rounds. R1 was an aptitude test (logic + quant + english). R2: resume screening. R3: puzzles round with interviewer, he gave me 3 puzzles: weighing 9 balls, the river crossing and a random probability one. R4: technical + stats round, asked about regression, correlation vs causation, sql select/join. R5: HR + manager chat, about why analytics, relocating to Bangalore and what i do for fun. Result was out after 2 days.
preparation: Puzzles on GFG for a week, stats from khan academy, SQL basics on w3schools.
experience: Pretty cool, honestly nothing too hard but lots of rounds. I enjoyed the puzzles.
advice: Prepare puzzles because they ask 2-3 at least. Know how to explain concepts simply.
tips: Mining students can do analytics, nobody cares about branch if u can think. Keep ur resume small.

selection: Schlumberger intern for Meta students, i think 5 rounds? R1 online aptitude (quant, logical, english). R2 resume shortlisting. R3 technical interview about core metallurgy: iron carbon diagram, TTT curves, heat treatment, difference between hardness and toughness, and corrosion types. R4 second technical interview with a senior engineer on failure analysis and welding metallurgy. R5 HR with questions about field work, relocation to Jamshedpur and my interest in oil and gas. Whole thing was 1 day, final selected people list around 10pm.
preparation: Core books (physical metallurgy and callister) + a 4 page notes on failure analysis. Aptitude from indiabix for 1 week.
experience: Good overall but long. Interviewers asked tough follow ups but were polite.
advice: Know everything in ur resume (esp project), and say honestly when u dont know.
tips: Practice speaking about technical concepts aloud. Ask seniors for HR tips. Carry water and snacks lol, no breaks.

selection: Fractal analyst intern for Chem students. R1 was an OA of 60 mins: aptitude, 2 sql queries and python mcqs. R2 was technical interview on ML basics (bias-variance, regularization, decision trees vs random forest, evaluation metrics) and my project on predicting reaction yield with regression, they liked that. R3 was HR + manager round, simple stuff. 3 rounds total. Result came within a day.
preparation: Learnt ML basics from andrew ng and did 2 kaggle projects. SQL from hackerrank.
experience: Good, interviewers appreciated the cross-disciplinary project.
advice: Show a domain-based ML project, it makes u stand out.
tips: Chem students, use ur domain data for projects (like process data). Don't do only titanic dataset projects pls.

selection: Amazon SDE/DS intern. R1: OA with 2 coding questions + work style assessment, 105 mins in total. I solved both questions (one on heap and one on dp). R2: first technical interview with 2 questions: a graph problem (number of islands variant) and a design of an LRU cache in code. R3: second technical, 2 more questions on trees and string, plus leadership principles questions (tell me about a time u failed, disagreed with someone etc). R4: bar-raiser type round with LPs heavy plus one DSA problem. Process lasted over 2 weeks. Got the offer on a Friday evening.
preparation: Did striver + leetcode amazon tagged questions, read all 16 leadership principles and prepared 6 stories. Had 5 mock interviews.
experience: Stressful but rewarding. Bar-raiser was the hardest. Feedback was nice afterwards.
advice: Prepare for LPs seriously, many people ignore it. Think out loud while solving.
tips: Write ur stories in STAR format and rehearse. Take care of ur health, interviews were close together. All the best!

selection: Schlumberger for EEE at campus, 5 rounds. R1 online aptitude plus basic EE mcqs (machines, power systems, network analysis). R2 resume shortlisting + a short GD. R3 technical interview: transformers (OC/SC test), induction motors (slip, torque slip curve), power factor correction, basic control systems and PLC. R4 technical 2 with project discussion (i did a solar inverter project), asked about harmonics and MPPT. R5 HR: field job acceptance, shifts, relocation to Jamshedpur. I had done an internship at SLB so PPO process was parallel, i got an offer from the PPO route too.
preparation: Revised EM, power systems, power electronics. Also practised aptitude, learnt about SLB operations.
experience: Tiring but ok. People were mostly kind.
advice: Know core EE fundamentals and ur project well. Field readiness is must.
tips: Intern at a company where u want to work, it helps with PPO. Take mock interviews with seniors from the same company.

selection: Schlumberger Mining placement had 3 rounds. R1: HR + aptitude screening (an online round of 40 mins). R2: technical interview: they asked about mine ventilation (fan laws, series and parallel), what is a stope, the difference between room and pillar and longwall, explosives and blasting patterns. R3: final HR round with a manager who asked about field postings, willingness for rotational work, how i handle stress in remote areas. Result the same night.
preparation: Core mining books and my notes, and a few mock interviews with a senior who was in oil and gas.
experience: Good. I was calm because i prepped core well. Interviewers were polite and a bit stern.
advice: Be flexible about field postings. Core + attitude is what they check.
tips: With a high cgpa (9+), shortlist is easier but interviews decide. Dont get overconfident. Revise 1st-2nd year fundamentals too.

selection: This is about my MS application (not a job). I applied to NUS for MS in Civil Engineering (structural/transportation track) coming from Mechanical, which made the profile a bit different so i had to justify it in my SOP. Application process: online portal with transcripts, CV, 2 SOP-type essays, 2 recommendation letters, GRE (not mandatory but i gave it) and IELTS. Deadline was in Dec-Jan window. After that there was no interview for me, only a result email after about 2.5 months. Decision came as admit with no scholarship initially.
preparation: GRE prep for 2 months (got 320+), IELTS 7.5 in one attempt. SOP drafts went through 5 versions with feedback from a senior and a prof. Two LORs from professors in my final-year project.
experience: Overall stressful because of waiting and the cost, but happy with the result.
advice: Show clearly why u are switching to civil (my project on structural vibration analysis helped). Apply early, check the department deadlines.
tips: Talk to seniors who got into NUS, ask for SOP samples. Start LOR requests 2 months before so profs have time. Dont ignore the funding options.
